name: Pin and trust images
objective: CKS › Supply Chain Security (20%). Drill EVERY supply-chain corner harder than the exam: Trivy CVE scanning with severity gates, static manifest analysis with kubesec, digest pinning, banning :latest, ImagePullPolicy hardening, an approved-registry ValidatingAdmissionPolicy + binding, a VAP that bans :latest, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix on a broken binding. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Pin an image by digest (@sha256:)
questions.teach:
A tag like `:1.36` is **mutable** — the registry owner can repoint it. A **digest** (`@sha256:<64 hex>`) is the hash of the exact image content, so it is **immutable**: the kubelet pulls precisely those bytes or fails. Pin with `image: busybox@sha256:<64 hex>`.

**Gotcha:** a digest is per-architecture — one copied from another arch won't pull on your node.
questions.prompt:
In `cks-supply`, create a pod `digest-pod` (container `app`, command `sleep 3600`) whose image is pinned **by digest** — `busybox@sha256:<64-hex-digest>` (any valid busybox digest).

Target: pod `digest-pod` exists; its container image is `busybox@sha256:` followed by a 64-char hex digest (not a plain tag).
questions.hint: Find a digest with `crane digest busybox:1.36` or `docker buildx imagetools inspect busybox:1.36`, or reuse a known one. Set `image: busybox@sha256:<64-hex>`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: digest-pod
  namespace: cks-supply
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox@sha256:9ae97d36d26566ff84e8893c64a6dc4fe8ca6d1144bf5b87b2b85a32def253c7
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
YAML

questions.title: Ban :latest — pin a real version + imagePullPolicy
questions.teach:
`:latest` floats to whatever was pushed last, so two deploys of the "same" image can run different code. Pin an explicit tag or digest, and set `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` so a pinned tag isn't silently re-pulled and swapped.

**Gotcha:** an **untagged** image (`nginx`) silently resolves to `nginx:latest` — just as bad as writing `:latest`.
questions.prompt:
In `cks-supply`, create a **Deployment** named `web` (1 replica, container `web`) whose image is a **pinned version** — NOT `:latest`, NOT untagged. Use `nginx:1.25-alpine`, and set `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` on the container.

Target: Deployment `web` exists; its container is named `web`, image carries an explicit tag (not `:latest`, not untagged) or `@sha256:`, and `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent`.
questions.hint: `kubectl create deployment web -n cks-supply --image=nginx:1.25-alpine` names the container `nginx`, not `web` — build YAML so the container is named `web`. Add `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web
  namespace: cks-supply
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector: { matchLabels: { app: web } }
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app: web } }
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: nginx:1.25-alpine
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
YAML

verification.description: Deployment web: container 'web', pinned image (not :latest), imagePullPolicy IfNotPresent

questions.title: Private-registry pull via imagePullSecrets
questions.teach:
Images from a private registry need credentials: create a `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` Secret with `kubectl create secret docker-registry`, then reference it under the pod spec's `imagePullSecrets`. The kubelet uses it to authenticate the pull.

**Gotcha:** `imagePullSecrets` lives on the **pod spec** (`spec.imagePullSecrets`), not on the container — and the Secret must be in the same namespace as the pod.
questions.prompt:
In `cks-supply`: (1) create a docker-registry Secret `regcred` for server `registry.internal:5000`, username `ci`, password `s3cr3t`; (2) create pod `private-pod` (image `busybox:1.36`, container `app`, `sleep 3600`) that references `regcred` under `spec.imagePullSecrets`.

Target: Secret `regcred` is type `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson`; pod `private-pod` lists `regcred` in `spec.imagePullSecrets`.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n cks-supply create secret docker-registry regcred --docker-server=registry.internal:5000 --docker-username=ci --docker-password=s3cr3t`. Then in the pod spec add `imagePullSecrets: [ { name: regcred } ]`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n cks-supply create secret docker-registry regcred \
  --docker-server=registry.internal:5000 --docker-username=ci --docker-password=s3cr3t
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: private-pod
  namespace: cks-supply
spec:
  imagePullSecrets:
  - name: regcred
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
YAML

verification.description: regcred dockerconfigjson Secret + private-pod referencing it in imagePullSecrets
